data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Correlated failures in decentralized networks are dominated by an 'ecological coincidence' mechanism: nodes do not fail because of a shared internal dependency, but because independent operators react identically to a shared external shock.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Operators face entirely heterogeneous environments and shocks, preventing synchronized responses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The external shock is so severe that both the centralized and decentralized networks fail completely regardless of response strategy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independent operators facing the same external environment (e.g., a sudden spike in traffic, a change in upstream API rate limits, a global supply chain shortage) will rationally deploy identical mitigation strategies (e.g., enabling aggressive rate limiting, shutting down non-essential endpoints). These synchronized rational responses cause simultaneous service degradation that looks like a shared internal failure but is actually an externally triggered correlation. The large service, having a unified command structure, can coordinate a localized response that sacrifices non-critical functions to save the core, avoiding system-wide failure.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
